newsitem.title: USA: Croatia has tentative loan agreement with IMF.
newsitem.headline: Croatia has tentative loan agreement with IMF.

text.p: Croatia has reached tentative agreement with the International Monetary Fund for a about a $500 million loan, Marko Skreb, governor of the National Bank of Croatia, told a briefing for reporters Wednesday.

Skreb and Borislav Skegro, Deputy Prime Minister for Commerce and Finance, told reporters that they expected the three-year extended fund facility loan to be approved by the IMF board in mid-March and used for structural reforms.

In addition, the two officials said that their country was close to completing an enterprise and financial sector adjustment loan from the World Bank to help rehabilitate some of the country's banks and restructure and privatize its large utilities. The country is also seeking to sell a $250 million eurobond issue with the closing and the pricing next week in London, Skreb told reporters.
The two officials said that Croatia had made substantial progress since independence, with the economy showing growth last year of about seven percent with relatively tame inflation.
They estimated that growth this year would remain in the six to seven percent range.
